metadata.note: The San Francisco and San Jose Railroad -- one of California's earliest railroads and the direct ancestor of today's Caltrain, which still runs on essentially this same alignment (see caltrain.geojson for the modern service). Incorporated 1860, one of the first railroads anywhere to employ Chinese laborers in its construction (beginning May 1861). Daily passenger service began October 18, 1863 between San Francisco (Valencia Street depot) and Mayfield (in modern south Palo Alto); the line reached San Jose's Market Street Depot on January 16, 1864, completing the full 49.5-mile route. Consolidated into the Southern Pacific in 1870, which ran it as the 'Peninsula Commute' for 110 years. Geometry is real-traced from OpenStreetMap active-rail geometry for the entire route -- unsurprising given this is still the exact corridor Caltrain runs today.
sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco_and_San_Jose_Railroad (incorporated 1860; construction began May 1861 using Chinese laborers; SF-Mayfield opened with daily service Oct 18 1863; completed to San Jose Jan 16 1864, 49.5 miles; consolidated into Southern Pacific 1870)

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peninsula_Commute (Southern Pacific operated this corridor as the Peninsula Commute 1870-1980; Caltrans subsidy 1980-1985; renamed Caltrain 1985, SP retained as contract operator; Peninsula Corridor Joint Powers Board purchased the right-of-way from SP in 1991)

Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.
